title: Reshape the four role profiles to fit the AC3 ceilings, never revise the targets (DEC-194 follow-up to LCLI-682)
description:
Follow-up to LCLI-682, filed under DEC-194 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1007), which chose A for #577: the measuring feature lands, and the profiles are brought within the AC3 ceilings separately. Ordinary under DEC-182. opum-doc's ruling, verbatim:

"The follow-up's HOW is decided: reshape the profiles, never revise the targets. This is the first evidence that the packs are wrong, not the targets.
(1) Profiles pin only the cli-contract sections their role needs, by anchor (MDL-8). The rest is reachable by exact-section expansion. Policy and role at or under 3k; authored bootstrap at or under 8k.
(2) Evidence selection is capped at the spec's 6k default maximum, highest-scoring first. Required content still over budget fails the compile (CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET, MDL-9) and is never dropped.
(3) Prove it on all four real profiles with the same command class, each under its AC3 ceilings. Any residual comes back to me with numbers and the content behind them.
ODOC-437 AC3 stays unchecked until (3) holds; the overrun is noted there."

MEASURED EVIDENCE AT FILING. `lore agent context review --task "review the context budget change to the role profiles" --json`, on the LCLI-682 report: policyAndRole target 3000 measured 10712 OVER; taskEvidence target 6000 measured 48180 OVER; loreSubtotal target 11000 measured 59926 OVER; AC3 authoredBootstrapCeiling 8000 measured 10712 OVER; AC3 taskEvidenceCeiling 16000 measured 48180 OVER. The pinned `reference/cli-contract` ALONE is ~10712 estimated tokens, so one whole-document pin exceeds both the policy-and-role target and the authored-bootstrap ceiling before any task evidence is selected. That is the "packs are wrong, not the targets" evidence.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each of the four real role profiles pins only the cli-contract sections its role needs, by anchor, so the compiled pack's policy-and-role is at or under 3k and its AC3 authored bootstrap at or under 8k.
Evidence selection is capped at the spec's 6k default maximum, highest-scoring first, and required content still over budget fails the compile rather than being dropped.
All four real profiles are measured with the same command class and each reports under its AC3 ceilings; any residual is reported to opum-doc with the numbers and the content behind them.

plan: CAP (DEC-194 (4) option A, one PR, cap FIRST). In the selection loop of compileAgentContext (src/core/agent-context.ts), admit a ranked candidate only while the EVIDENCE tier's own running total stays within the profile's declared `[targets].task_evidence`. Highest-scoring first is already what `ordered` is. A profile that declares NO `[targets]` keeps today's behaviour EXACTLY -- no hidden cap, because lore is public and a silent one would surprise external users. The declared value is 6000 in all four real profiles.

REQUIRED CONTENT OVER THE CAP FAILS, never dropped: a new CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET error, alongside the existing CONTEXT_REQUIRED_SOURCE_MISSING naming convention. In the evidence tier the required content is the bundle's Constitution when a profile RANKS it in `sources` (the code already treats that one as mandatory policy and keeps it at zero score). If it cannot fit the cap, the compile fails naming the profile, the budget and the required size, rather than silently omitting it.

BREADCRUMB REPORTING (approved scope, reporting field only). `budgetEntry`'s content currently records `item.reference`, which for a section-level candidate is the CONCEPT -- so a 110-section budget reads as 13 repeated concept ids and cannot deliver the residual 'with the content behind it' that DEC-194 (3) asks for. Record the section's breadcrumb alongside the reference. Include the measured cost in the PR: those names are RENDERED into the pack by budgetLine, and the taskEvidence list is 3659 chars ~ 914 tokens today; after the cap it is ~13 entries, which is why the cap goes first.

SPEC AMENDMENT, NET ZERO. docs/specs/agent-profile-context-retrieval.md currently says targets are 'NOT ceilings enforced before a request'. That becomes false for task_evidence once selection is capped, so amend it in place: task_evidence is ENFORCED for selection when declared, the other three classes stay measurement-only. It is a PINNED source of `implementation` and named by others, so it ships net zero against the capacities, paid for in the same section, and `lore check` must exit 0.

PROOFS, both ways where the ruling names a both-ways: a profile WITH `[targets]` caps selection at its declared task_evidence; a profile with NO `[targets]` selects exactly as today (no cap); required content over the cap FAILS with CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET rather than being dropped; and a capping profile's budget report names the section, not the concept. Mutation controls for each.

BEFORE/AFTER per profile on the MERGED state, never moving a target: document, implementation, review, verification, measured with the same command class the task was filed from (`lore agent context <profile> --task "review the context budget change to the role profiles" --json`). Any residual goes back to the leader with the numbers and the content behind them.

The PROFILE RESHAPE (DEC-194 (1): pin cli-contract SECTIONS by anchor, policy_and_role <= 3000, authored bootstrap <= 8000) is the NEXT PR, not this one -- measured separately because it needs the anchor form `reference/cli-contract#5-failure-model`, verified to resolve.
implementationNotes:
HANDOFF — session renewal, 2026-10-14. The successor continues LCLI-722 from the DEC-194 (5) boundary; this note plus the record above it is the whole brief.

STATE. Branch feat/LCLI-722-evidence-cap, head 1f7251b9a5515c370186cbb4f3840ddfbd043407, pushed. PR opum-ai/lore-cli#592 is OPEN and HELD at the leader's instruction for a delta re-review; NOT merged. The dev merge is already IN the branch (6970b101), so the branch is one commit ahead of origin/dev. Review worktree was re-pointed: .claude/worktrees/lore-cli-review-722 at that head.

WHAT LANDED on this branch, in order: c9295325 (the cap, the required-content failure, the section labels), 8492f13b (the first addendum's assertions), 6970b101 (dev merged in), 48132414 (delta fixes — spec churn reverted to a SINGLE HUNK, the converse assertion made falsifiable, the zero-score floor made honest), 1f7251b9 (DEC-194 (5) option A: required content reserved against BOTH budgets before ranked evidence is admitted, plus the non-blocking fixes and the LCLI-731 filing). LCLI-728 landed separately as squash f93d5a23 and is CLOSED. origin/main is untouched at 19c88460 — no promotion; the lore+quest pair release owns that.

WHAT THE RE-REVIEW SHOULD COVER: the delta c9295325..1f7251b9, with the dev merge excluded. Named checks already handed to reviewers, and they are the three things not to accept on the code's say-so: (i) the synthetic-bundle proof's non-vacuity — count floors, the converse, and its mutation; (ii) the LCLI-680 re-expression, which is a REAL COVERAGE LOSS rather than a tidy-up (with the cap on, NO real-profile source is omitted-by-relevance, so LCLI-680's relevance/budget distinction is proved only on the synthetic fixture now); (iii) the spec amendment, which sits EXACTLY on the file's 19-token headroom.

WITH opum-doc, not mine to settle: the LCLI-680 real-profile witness loss, the timeout-under-load measurement (a mutation table initially credited a load timeout to three code mutations — each file now runs in its own invocation), and the breadcrumb correction (inert on the evidence tier once the cap lands; it earns its place on the pinned tier after the reshape).

ORDER AFTER #592: LCLI-730 (the DEC-192 (8) load-time warning; it still owes one non-blocking scoping note relayed by the leader — the DEC-192 (1) test should say which fixture it holds for), then LCLI-729, then LCLI-731, then the PROFILE RESHAPE (DEC-194 (1)) — the second half of LCLI-722 and the thing that removes the whole-document cli-contract pin. The reshape also frees ~7.7k tokens of policyAndRole headroom, which is where the spec clause dropped for space — "skipping rather than stopping" — should land, at net zero, since it does not fit today.

LANDMINES FOR THE SUCCESSOR, all measured this session. (a) THE CAPACITY GATE IS AT ITS CEILING: implementation renders 110621 tokens against a 111000 budget with a 360-token query-section reserve, so `docs/specs/agent-profile-context-retrieval.md` has 19 TOKENS (76 bytes) of headroom and ANY growth there reddens `agent-profile-capacity`; the amendment is +76 bytes exactly. (b) `git worktree remove` FAILS with Permission denied on review worktrees here — chmod -R u+w, rm -rf, `git worktree prune`, then re-add; the failed remove deregisters the worktree while leaving the directory, so the re-add then refuses with "already exists". (c) This handoff note lands on a tracker-only branch, so #592 will need a further dev merge that touches .quest/tasks/LCLI-722.json. (d) The INSTALLED `lore` is stale and reports a false red for `lore check` in this repository; `bun run lore check` from source is the gate, and CI runs that.

REACH FOR: the opum-sdlc skill for branch/PR/land and its references/quest-writes.md; opum-handoff restore on resume; and the standing pre-filing check `quest task list --across-refs` before creating any task, which is how LCLI-731's id was allocated after reading every open PR head.

DELTA FIX (session 2026-10-14, restored from the handoff note above). Branch feat/LCLI-722-evidence-cap, PR opum-ai/lore-cli#592. dev ef41f1e1 merged in (tracker-only; .quest/tasks/LCLI-722.json resolved to dev side, which was a strict superset of this branch empty notes).

THE DELTA REVIEW BLOCKING ITEM IS FIXED. queryHitLimit and querySection were sized against build([]) (pins only) while the mandatory floor was build(required, queryHitLimit, querySection), so the reserve a query section claimed against a pins-only pack was also charged to the mandatory-content floor. A budget B with pins + hits <= B < pins + Constitution + hits, and pins + Constitution <= B, THREW although the required content alone fits: the DEC-194 (5) exception fired where its own condition did not hold, and the query section turned a compiling pack into a failure, breaking the rule stated with the mandatory-pin floor. Now the required candidates are computed BEFORE the query section is sized, both the shrink loop and the why-line test measure build(required, n), and the floor is build(required, 0, false) — required content with NO query section at all.

PROOF, both ways and mutation-tested. The new test asserts the INVARIANT that the smallest compiling budget is the same with the query section as without it (compileAgentContextWithoutQueryHits, no section at all), with the roomy pack carrying all 3 hits and the floor pack carrying 0, so the fixture genuinely squeezes a section rather than never having one. On the pre-fix sizing that test reddens: 1007 against 912, a 95-token gap, and the other 24 tests in the file stay green. One token below the floor still fails CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET, so the exception is proved NARROWED rather than removed.

Also the three non-blocking items: the half-stale exempt-from-the-CAP paragraph is deleted (the loop no longer skips required candidates), the throw now names the floor figure alongside the candidate sum, and the CHANGELOG long line is re-wrapped with the first-revision clause dropped. Clause (c), skips rather than stops, is NOT here — deferred to the profile-reshape PR by the leader decision.

Gates on the merged tree: bun test 5120 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail (5123 tests, 150 files); typecheck exit 0; lint exit 0; bun run lore check exit 0, 4 agent profiles read, 0 over capacity.
